subject: Architecture
title: The Sydney Harbour Bridge: The Coathanger
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Sydney Harbour Bridge: The Coathanger.

hook.text: Sydney's Harbour Bridge is the world's largest steel arch bridge — nicknamed 'The Coathanger.'

buildup.text: Its arch spans 1,650 feet and carries eight traffic lanes, two rail lines, a bike path, and a footpath.

discovery.text: The arch was built from both sides simultaneously. Temporary cables held each half until they met.

twist.text: Six million rivets hold the bridge together — each one heated, hammered in by hand, and checked.

climax.text: Today tourists can climb to the top of the arch — 440 feet above the harbor — for panoramic views.

punchline.text: Six million rivets, two halves, one coathanger. Sydney's most loved landmark.

quiz.question: How many rivets hold the Sydney Harbour Bridge together?

details.summary: The Sydney Harbour Bridge, opened in 1932, is one of the world's widest long-span bridges, carrying eight traffic lanes, two rail lines, a footway, and a cycleway on its 49-meter-wide deck. Its steel arch spans 503 meters and required six million hand-driven rivets during construction.
details.whyItMatters: The Sydney Harbour Bridge defined its city's identity more than any other structure. It demonstrated that bridges are not just transportation — they become the iconic symbols that represent entire cities to the world.
takeaways: Opened in 1932 with one of the widest bridge decks in the world
The steel arch spans 503 meters and used six million rivets
It carries roads, rail, pedestrians, and cyclists simultaneously

faq.question: Why is it called the Coathanger?
faq.answer: Its arch profile resembles a coat hanger when viewed from the side. Sydneysiders adopted the nickname affectionately shortly after it opened. The distinctive shape has become one of the world's most recognized architectural silhouettes alongside the Sydney Opera House.

faq.question: Can you climb the Sydney Harbour Bridge?
faq.answer: Yes. BridgeClimb Sydney has offered guided climbs to the summit since 1998. Climbers ascend the outer arch to the top, 134 meters above the harbor. Over four million people have completed the climb, making it one of the world's most popular adventure tourism experiences.
